artists.biography:
Ray Charles Robinson (September 23, 1930 - June 10, 2004), known by his shortened stage name Ray Charles, was an American musician. He was a pioneer in the genre of soul music during the 1950s by fusing rhythm and blues, gospel, and blues styles into his early recordings with Atlantic Records. He also helped racially integrate country and pop music during the 1960s with his crossover success on ABC Records, most notably with his Modern Sounds albums. While with ABC, Charles became one of the first African-American musicians to be given artistic control by a mainstream record company. Frank Sinatra called Charles "the only true genius in show business".

The influences upon his music were mainly jazz, blues, rhythm and blues and country artists of the day such as Art Tatum, Nat King Cole, Louis Jordan, Charles Brown, Louis Armstrong. His playing reflected influences from country blues and barrelhouse, and stride piano styles.
Rolling Stone ranked Charles number ten on their list of "100 Greatest Artists of All Time" in 2004, and number two on their November 2008 list of "100 Greatest Singers of All Time". In honoring Charles, Billy Joel noted: "This may sound like sacrilege, but I think Ray Charles was more important than Elvis Presley. I don't know if Ray was the architect of rock & roll, but he was certainly the first guy to do a lot of things . . . Who the hell ever put so many styles together and made it work?"

perplexity.description:
The Atlantic Years – In Mono is a comprehensive 7-LP box set compiling Ray Charles’s seminal work recorded for Atlantic Records between 1952 and 1959. Originally released as individual albums between 1957 and 1961, the collection showcases Charles’s groundbreaking fusion of gospel, blues, jazz, and R&B, laying the foundation for what would later be recognized as soul music. The set includes landmark albums such as Ray Charles, The Great Ray Charles, The Genius Sings the Blues, and What’d I Say, featuring classics like “I Got a Woman,” “Hallelujah I Love Her So,” and the title track “What’d I Say.” Charles’s innovative approach—translating the ecstatic fervor of gospel into secular pop—was both controversial and revolutionary, helping to break down musical and racial barriers in 1950s America.

Musically, the box set highlights Charles’s dynamic range, from the exuberant energy of “Night Time Is the Right Time” to the introspective melancholy of “Drown In My Own Tears.” The recordings capture his evolution as a vocalist, pianist, and bandleader, with each album reflecting his growing technical mastery and artistic vision. While most of the material was originally released in mono, the set’s remastered vinyl pressings preserve the raw, intimate sound that defined Charles’s Atlantic years. Critically, these albums are regarded as some of the most influential in American popular music, with “What’d I Say” frequently cited as one of the greatest rock and roll songs of all time. Commercially, the Atlantic years marked Charles’s rise to national prominence, setting the stage for his later success and cementing his legacy as a pioneer of soul.
